title: A MORAL- AND EVENT- CENTRIC INSPECTION OF GENDER BIAS IN FAIRY TALES AT A LARGE SCALE
findings: Female characters are more associated with sanctity-related moral words, a dimension defined as including 'spiritual concerns'. The paper does not provide further interpretation of this finding in a religious or faith-based context, focusing instead on broader gender stereotypes.

measurement_description: The paper uses the 'sanctity/degradation' moral foundation, which concerns 'moral disgust and spiritual concerns related to the body', to analyze gender bias in fairy tales. The analysis does not focus on specific religious themes or groups but on the general moral framing associated with characters.
